candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — respiratory comfort measures and postoperative care
candidate.educational_objective: Demonstrate correct slow, sustained inspiratory technique when using an incentive spirometer.

options.A: Inhale rapidly and forcefully through the device, then exhale into the mouthpiece.
options.B: Use only normal tidal breaths because deep inspiration is not intended.
options.C: Inhale slowly and deeply through the mouthpiece, hold the breath briefly at maximal inspiration, then exhale normally away from the mouthpiece.
options.D: Exhale forcefully into the device because incentive spirometry primarily trains expiration.

candidate.rationale: Incentive spirometry is an inspiratory maneuver. The client should inhale slowly and deeply through the mouthpiece, sustain maximal inspiration briefly, then remove the mouthpiece and exhale normally. It should be part of a broader postoperative pulmonary-care plan rather than relied on alone. Therefore C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Correct incentive-spirometer use uses a slow deep inspiration through the mouthpiece with a brief inspiratory hold, followed by relaxed exhalation after removing the mouthpiece; incentive spirometry is not a standalone postoperative prevention strategy.
